Read the National Pedon Database of Canada

Source: R/npdb.R
load_npdb_pedons.Rd

Reads the pre-packaged CSV files of the National Pedon Database (NPDB, version 3, Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada, CanSIS) into PedonRecord objects, with the survey's classification under the Canadian System of Soil Classification as the reference.

Usage

load_npdb_pedons(dir, max_n = NULL, seed = NULL, verbose = TRUE)

Arguments

dir

Folder with the NPDB CSV files.

max_n

Optional maximum number of pedons (a random sample).

seed

Optional seed for that sample.

verbose

Print progress.

Value

A named list of PedonRecord objects (names are the NPDB PEDON_ID).

Details

The NPDB is not distributed with soilKey. It is published on the Open Government Portal of Canada under the Open Government Licence - Canada (dataset "National Pedon Database"); download the pre-packaged CSV files and unzip them into a folder. Info.csv and Horizons.csv are required; Morphology.csv, Physical.csv, Chemical.csv and Profiles.csv are read when present.

What the reader does with the records:

  • records are split on CR-LF only, since some fields hold a lone carriage return ("subangular\r blocky");

  • the designation is rebuilt in the Canadian notation from its parts (lithologic numeral, master, suffixes, numeric modifier: "IICk1"), and the site declares designation_system = "cssc";

  • depths: organic and water horizons recorded upward from the mineral surface (top above bottom) become negative depths; a mineral horizon with its depths reversed or negative keeps |top| with no bottom when it is the deepest layer, and no depths otherwise; a missing top is taken from the layer above; every profile is shifted to begin at 0 cm, and site$npdb_depth_order_mismatch flags profiles whose depth order differs from the order of their layers;

  • colours: the codes ("100yr4030", "10yr2010", "025y 4020", "10.0yr4.0/3.0", "n 50") are read with hue numbers above 0 and up to 10; of the two matrix colours, the one that is never darker within a profile (and lighter at least once) is read as the dry colour and the other as the moist one; when they do not separate, COLOUR_1 is read as the moist colour and no dry colour is read;

  • total N: the value 9 (a no-data code) and a value repeated over three or more horizons are not read; the units are told apart by the median C:N of each pedon (of its dataset when the pedon has too few values): 5 to 40 is read as percent, 0.5 to 4 as g/kg (divided by 10), anything else is not read; a horizon whose C:N then lies outside 3 to 60 is not read either;

  • base saturation: computed from the exchangeable bases and the CEC (at most 100 %) when they are recorded, the recorded value being kept when it agrees with it (one dataset records something else in that column);

  • pH: a dataset whose pH in CaCl2 is mostly above its pH in water has the two columns swapped back;

  • values outside their possible range are not read;

  • the survey's order, great group and subgroup words are turned into the names of the 3rd edition (1998) where they match one (reference_cssc_order, reference_cssc_great_group, reference_cssc_subgroup), including the subgroups the 1998 edition merged (Solodic into Solonetzic); names of earlier editions with no 1998 equivalent are left out, and the raw words are kept in reference_cssc_raw.

The NPDB records no soil climate (mean annual soil temperature, moisture subclass), the chemistry of the podzolic B (pyrophosphate-extractable Fe and Al) or the contrast of mottles. The Chernozemic order and the Gray Brown Luvisols, which ask for the climate, are undecided on these records (see benchmark_npdb).

References

Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada (2021). National Pedon Database, version 3. Open Government Portal, Open Government Licence - Canada.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
peds <- load_npdb_pedons("path/to/npdb_v3_csv")
b <- benchmark_npdb(peds, level = "order")
b$accuracy
} # }
